correctness.rationale: The exact radial moment formulas give boundary-minus-bulk displacement ε²/(4π) times the integral of exp(iθ)((f′)²−2f²), plus O_f(ε³); the stated gauges cancel both first variations. The ordered Fourier pairs give exactly Q, and Parseval gives deficit 8π²ε²E+O_f(ε³), with E>0 and L→2π. For b_k=√(k²−1)a_k the adjacent form uses weight γ_k=√((k−1)(k+2)/(k(k+1)))<1 tending to 1. Strictness follows by Cauchy–Schwarz with a strict weight on any nonzero adjacent product; if none, Q=0. Real equal-energy consecutive packets, taken arbitrarily long and high, approach the bound. Indeed normalized almost-maximizers lose all mass on any fixed initial band: writing d_k=|b_k| and d_1=0, the sum of (d_{k+1}−d_k)² equals 2(1−Σ d_k d_{k+1}) and tends to zero. If all consecutive nonzero runs had length bounded by r, the path adjacency Rayleigh bound gives Σ d_k d_{k+1}≤cos(π/(r+1))<1. Positivity of the radial curvature numerator holds separately for each fixed test function. This proves the strict fixed-f limit, supremum, nonattainment and single-mode statement without a finite quadrature test.
